readme:
# Steam Store Scraper

Search the Steam store for games and get one clean row per game: title, price, discount, release date, review score, platforms and, optionally, the full store details such as developers, publishers, genres, languages, Metacritic score and screenshots. You can also look up games directly by app id or store URL.

The data comes from the public Steam store pages and the public store API. No login and no API key are needed.

## What you get

For each game the actor returns:

- Identity: app id, store URL, title, item type (App, Sub or Bundle)
- Price: current price, price before discount, discount percent, currency, and the price text as the store shows it
- Reviews: review label (for example "Very Positive"), percent positive, number of reviews
- Release: release date as the store shows it, and whether the game is still coming soon
- Platforms: Windows, Mac, Linux
- With details on: developers, publishers, genres, categories, short description, full description text, supported languages, languages with full audio, Metacritic score and link, recommendation count, achievement count, required age, DLC ids, website, support page and email, content notes, minimum PC requirements, header image, screenshots and trailers

Fields the store does not show for a game are returned as null.

## Pricing

You pay per delivered game. There is also a small start fee, charged once per run together with the first delivered game. Nothing is charged for a run that finds no games.

| Event name | When it is charged | Price |
|---|---|---|
| `actor-start` | Once per run, with the first delivered game | $0.001 per run |
| `steam-game-result` | For each game row delivered | $0.0006 per game ($0.60 per 1,000) |

If you set a maximum charge for the run, the actor stops cleanly when the limit is reached and keeps the games already delivered.

## Input

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `searchTerms` | list of text | Words to search in the store |
| `appIds` | list of text | Steam app ids to look up directly |
| `startUrls` | list of text | Store game page URLs, the app id is read from the URL |
| `country` | text | Two-letter store country code. Sets prices and currency. Default `us` |
| `maxResultsPerQuery` | number | Games per search term, 1 to 1000. Default 50 |
| `includeDetails` | true or false | Add the full store details to each game. Default true |

An empty input runs a small demo: search "strategy", 5 games.

### Example: search two terms

```json
{
  "searchTerms": ["strategy", "roguelike"],
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 60,
  "includeDetails": true,
  "country": "us"
}
```

### Example: price check in euros, list only

```json
{
  "searchTerms": ["city builder"],
  "maxResultsPerQuery": 100,
  "includeDetails": false,
  "country": "de"
}
```

### Example: look up specific games

```json
{
  "appIds": ["570", "289070"],
  "startUrls": ["https://store.steampowered.com/app/1245620/ELDEN_RING/"],
  "country": "gb"
}
```

  "developers": ["Square Enix", "ARTDINK"],

The sample is shortened. Each row has the same set of fields, listed in the dataset schema.

## FAQ

**How fast is it?**
With details on, the actor reads about one game every 1.6 seconds, because the store limits how quickly details can be requested. A run of 100 games takes about three minutes. With details off, a page of 50 games takes about a second.

**What does `details_status` mean?**
`ok` means the full details were read. `unavailable` means the store has no public data for that app. `failed` means the details could not be read after retries. `not_requested` means you switched details off.

**Why are some games listed without a price?**
Games that are not released yet often show no price. The price fields are null for them. Free games show `is_free` true.

**Are prices in my currency?**
Prices follow the `country` setting. Use `de` for euro prices, `gb` for pound prices, and so on. Prices are given in the smallest currency unit (cents) and as the text the store shows.

**Can I get user reviews?**
This actor returns the review summary (label, percent and count). It does not return single review texts.

**Why did my run return fewer games than I asked for?**
The store may have fewer matches for the term, or the maximum charge for the run was reached. The run status message says which.

**Is the same game returned twice if two search terms match it?**
No. Each game is returned once per run, under the first search term that found it.

**What happens if the run is interrupted and restarted?**
The actor saves its progress after every batch of games and continues from there, without repeating games or charging twice.

**Is it allowed to scrape Steam?**
The actor reads publicly visible store pages and the public store API at a low request rate. You are responsible for using the data in line with the store terms and the laws that apply to you.
